data_section_full_text:
3. Data and method
Data sources
We identify all available firm-years for Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) listed
firms contained in the Aspect Financial data base with a June 30 year-end, from
1993 through 2000. <sup><u>11</u></sup> We begin with years ending June 30, 1993 for two reasons.


CAR Vol. 23 No. 3 (Fall 2006)

Nonaudit Services and Earnings Conservatism 711

First, AASB 1026, “Statement of Cash Flows”, applied to financial years ending
on or after June 30, 1992, thereby allowing us to observe operating cash flow
( CFOit ) directly, rather than infer it by means of the indirect method (Hribar and
Collins 2002). Second, AASB 1018, “Income Statement”, applied to years ending
on or after December 31, 1992. This standard tightened the definition of extraordinary items and was operative for the entire period from which our data are drawn,
thereby ensuring that operating profit ( OIit ) and net profit ( NIit ) are consistently
defined across the entire sample period. Share price data are obtained from the
Share Price and Price relative (SPPR) data base maintained at the University of Western Australia, and details of auditor identity, audit fees, and NAS fees are obtained
from Who Audits Australia? (Craswell 2001) or, alternatively, hand-collected from
annual reports. After deleting all observations for firms in the financial services
industry, we have a total of 4,061 firm-year observations with all necessary data.
We further exclude extreme observations for any of our accounting variables or
stock return variables (that is, those values in the top or bottom 1 percent of the
sample), leaving a final sample of 3,746 firm-years for which we have all the necessary data
